prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1482; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change. Insured vehicle reported contact with the claimant's vehicle on the driver's side rear quarter panel. Claimant reports neck and back strain and states they were seen at an urgent care facility the same day. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Initial contact made by phone; claimant agreed to provide photos and a written statement.

Entry 2: Received claimant's written statement and photographs of vehicle damage. Statement describes the other vehicle drifting into the claimant's lane without signaling. Photos show scraping along the rear passenger side and a cracked taillight lens. Claimant confirms no prior neck or back complaints in the past several years. Insured's statement obtained and consistent with the claimant's account on the lane change, though insured disputes the amount of lateral contact.

Entry 3: Obtained urgent care records. Diagnosis listed as cervical and lumbar strain with prescribed muscle relaxants and a referral to physical therapy. No fractures or imaging performed. Claimant has begun a physical therapy schedule of two visits per week. Reviewed the scene diagram provided by the insured and noted that a witness was identified but has not yet responded to contact attempts.

Entry 4: Sent claimant a letter explaining the claims process, the coverage limits that apply, and the option to seek legal advice should they wish. Claimant called to ask about rental car coverage and was advised of the terms on their policy. Collision repair estimate received from the appraiser and forwarded to the claimant for review. Claimant has not yet indicated agreement with the estimate.

Entry 5: Physical therapy progress notes received and reviewed. Claimant reports improvement in range of motion but continued stiffness when driving more than thirty minutes. Witness reached by phone and confirmed seeing the other vehicle move into the adjacent lane without signaling. Claim file updated with liability assessment favoring the other driver. Next step is to review the physical therapy discharge summary when it becomes available and reassess the bodily injury evaluation.
